title: Valuative existence implies universal closedness for quasi-compact algebraic-space morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Assume $f$ is quasi-compact: for every affine scheme $T\to Y$, the point space $|X\times_YT|$ is quasi-compact. Suppose that for every valuation ring $A$ with fraction field $K$ [def-trf-valuation-ring] and every commutative square $u:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$, $v:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ with $fu=v|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$, there are a field extension $K\subset K'$, a valuation ring $A'\subset K'$ with fraction field $K'$ containing and dominating $A$, and $w:\operatorname{Spec}A'\to X$ such that $fw=v\circ\operatorname{Spec}(A\to A')$ and $w|_{\operatorname{Spec}K'}=u\circ\operatorname{Spec}(K\to K')$. Dominating means $\mathfrak m_{A'}\cap A=\mathfrak m_A$. Then $f$ is universally closed: for every algebraic space $Y'\to Y$, the induced map $|X\times_Y Y'|\to|Y'|$ is closed.

source.place: Tag 03KA (lemma-quasi-compact-existence-universally-closed); existence with field extension as in Tag 03IX (definition-valuative-criterion).

proof.text: Fix an affine scheme $T\to Y$ and put $P=X\times_YT$, with projection $p:P\to T$. The sheaf fibre product exists by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The hypothesis on quasi-compactness gives that $|P|$ is quasi-compact. The existence hypothesis also holds for $p$: compose a valuation square for $p$ with $P\to X$ and $T\to Y$, apply the hypothesis to $f$, and pair the resulting map $\operatorname{Spec}A\prime\to X$ with the prescribed composite $\operatorname{Spec}A\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$. Their composites to $Y$ agree, so the fibre-product universal property gives a map to $P$; on the fraction field its two components are precisely the original generic map after extension.

source.place: Tag 03KA, first paragraph; base-change existence argument of Tag 03IY (lemma-base-change-valuative-criteria).

proof.text: Choose an affine scheme $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and a surjective etale atlas $a:U\to P$ using [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. For a closed subset $C\subseteq|P|$, the subset $D=|a|^{-1}(C)$ is closed because $|a|$ is continuous [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$. The composite $g=p a:U\to T$ is the spectrum of a ring map $R\to B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Surjectivity gives $g(D)=p(C)$: a point of $C$ has a preimage in $U$, and every point of $D$ maps into $C$. It remains to show that this common image is stable under specialization.

source.place: Tag 03KA, affine etale atlas and inverse image of a closed subset.

proof.text: Let $y\prime\in p(C)$ specialize to $y\in T$. Choose $x\prime\in C$ over $y\prime$ and a representative $u:\operatorname{Spec}K\to P$ of this point; representatives and invariance under common field extension are [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-specialization-prescribed-field-probe] to the scheme morphism $p u:\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ and $y$. It gives a valuation subring $A\subseteq K$ and $v:\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$ with special point $y$ and generic restriction $p u$. Step 1 supplies $K\subseteq K\prime$, a dominating valuation ring $A\prime$ and $w:\operatorname{Spec}A\prime\to P$ extending $u$. If $s\prime=\mathfrak m_{A\prime}$, domination means that its image in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $\mathfrak m_A$, so $p(w(s\prime))=y$. In the spectrum of the domain $A\prime$, $(0)\subseteq\mathfrak m_{A\prime}$ says that the generic point specializes to $s\prime$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Continuity of $|w|$ [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] makes $w(s\prime)$ a specialization of $x\prime$; the generic image is still $x\prime$ by field-point equivalence. Since $C$ is closed, $w(s\prime)\in C$. Thus $y\in p(C)$.

source.place: Tag 03KA, second paragraph: valuation domination and specialization lifting, using Tag 01J8 to package the local-ring construction.

proof.text: By step 3, $g(D)=p(C)$ is stable under specialization, and $D$ is closed by step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-spectrum-specialization-stable-image-closed] to the ring map $R\to B$ and $D$. It follows that $p(C)$ is closed for every closed $C\subseteq|P|$. As the affine test $T\to Y$ was arbitrary, [lem-sfb-space-universally-closed-affine-tests] now proves that $f$ is universally closed.

source.place: Tag 03KA, conclusion using Tag 00HY; affine test criterion Tag 03IT.
